title: KmerSignificance score: A discriminative and biologically informed framework for viral k-mer prioritization.
abstract: Distinguishing closely related viral strains requires identifying genomic regions where subtle sequence differences carry biological significance. While k-mer-based approaches offer computational efficiency for genome analysis, existing methods lack standardized frameworks for evaluating which k-mers are most informative. Current selection strategies focus primarily on statistical discriminative power without integrating biological context. We introduce KmerSignificance Score (KSS), a k-mer prioritization framework combining three components: an information-theoretic method measuring strain-distinguishing capacity, an optimized amino acid substitution matrix (MIYATA_EVO) for mutation impact assessment, and a protein characterization score derived from annotations and database cross-references retrieved through UniProt. All three component scores and the integrated KSS are bounded in [0,1] by construction, providing a common numerical scale for ranking positions within a dataset. The discriminative component achieved a mean F1 of 0.881, not significantly different from chi-squared (0.876), the strongest of eight baselines. Top-ranked selections from the discriminative component nonetheless differed from those produced by chi-squared, especially for SARS-CoV-2 and HIV-1. The MIYATA_EVO matrix, optimized using a genetic algorithm, increased the composite agreement score across eight amino acid characteristics by 28.4% over the original MIYATA matrix. Across 17,471 viral proteins, the protein characterization score tracked UniProt's five-level annotation score closely (Kendall's τ=0.775), as expected for measures drawing on overlapping annotation content. Within each level, the continuous score provided finer numerical resolution among proteins. Literature cross-referencing on SARS-CoV-2 (278,738 sequences, 19 Pango-derived lineage labels), HIV-1 (12,223 sequences, 15 subtype labels), and human cytomegalovirus (HCMV; 399-646 sequences, 4-8 locus-specific genotypes) found that the top-ranked k-mers reported here map to established variant-defining mutations, subtype-specific polymorphisms, and genotype markers. KSS provides a standardized framework for viral k-mer prioritization with potential applications in variant surveillance, molecular epidemiology, and functional annotation. The tool is available at https://github.com/bioinfoUQAM/KmerSignificanceScore.

title: Temporal Changes in Antimicrobial Resistance, SpvB Polyproline Linker Length, and Pulsed-Field Gel Electrophoresis Types of
abstract: Fowl typhoid, caused by Salmonella Gallinarum (SG), remains an important poultry disease. We characterized 136 SG isolates, one per farm, from diagnostic submissions of diseased chickens to the national veterinary laboratory in South Korea from 2002 to 2026, comparing two periods (2002-2010 and 2011-2026). Antimicrobial susceptibility was determined by broth microdilution, the spvB polyproline linker (PPL; the region joining the two functional domains of the SpvB virulence factor) was sequenced, and genetic relatedness was assessed by XbaI-pulsed-field gel electrophoresis (PFGE). Resistance to nalidixic acid was most frequent (93.4%), followed by streptomycin (83.1%) and ciprofloxacin (71.3%). Resistance to ampicillin, tetracycline, and nalidixic acid was less frequent in 2011-2026 (false discovery rate-adjusted p < 0.05), and these associations persisted after adjustment for chicken type. Multidrug resistance was detected in 52.2% of isolates, without significant change between periods. However, 13 of the 34 multidrug-resistant isolates from 2002-2010 were resistant to four or more antimicrobial classes, whereas all 37 from 2011-2026 were resistant to exactly three classes. Five PPL lengths of 13-21 prolines were identified, and their distribution differed between periods (p = 0.016). Isolates carrying ≥17 prolines were more frequent in 2011-2026 than in 2002-2010 (p < 0.01). PFGE yielded 61 pulsotypes in 27 clusters, with two dominant clusters detected across years and chicken types. These findings indicate that the PFGE-defined SG population showed temporal phenotypic changes within Korean poultry flocks, underscoring the need for continued surveillance of resistance and genotype.

title: Molecular Characterization of Lumpy Skin Disease Virus in Bulgaria: Phylogenetic Insights Based on the RPO30 Gene.
abstract: Capripoxviruses are important viral pathogens of domestic ruminants and include lumpy skin disease virus (LSDV), sheeppox virus (SPPV), and goatpox virus (GTPV). In recent years, the spread of LSDV into Southeastern Europe has renewed interest in its molecular epidemiology, particularly in Balkan countries. This study analyzed partial RPO30 gene sequences obtained from clinical samples collected during the 2016 LSDV outbreak in Bulgaria. Viral DNA was detected by real-time PCR, and RPO30 amplicons obtained by conventional PCR were subjected to Sanger sequencing. The obtained sequences were compared with representative LSDV reference sequences retrieved from GenBank, and phylogenetic relationships were reconstructed using the Maximum Likelihood method. The five Bulgarian sequences included in the final analysis were positioned near Balkan and Neethling-type LSDV reference sequences and showed high sequence similarity within the analyzed partial RPO30 region. Single nucleotide polymorphisms enabled differentiation among the analyzed sequences and revealed limited variation within the Bulgarian sequence set. Haplotype analysis identified 10 haplotypes across the final 30-sequence dataset; however, all haplotype, SNP, distance-based, and phylogenetic results derive from the same partial RPO30 marker and were interpreted accordingly. The data provide additional information on the molecular characteristics of the analyzed Bulgarian LSDV sequences from the 2016 outbreak, while emphasizing the need for higher-resolution genomic approaches for recombinant or vaccine-like strain characterization and fine-scale epidemiological inference.

title: Comparative Mitogenomics Reveals Mitochondrial Diversity of
abstract: Haemonchus contortus is a highly pathogenic hematophagous gastrointestinal nematode and one of the most important constraints to small-ruminant health and productivity worldwide, causing anemia, reduced weight gain, decreased milk production, and substantial economic losses. Understanding its genetic diversity and population structure is essential for improving parasite surveillance and informing sustainable control strategies. In this study, individual H. contortus larvae collected from Pakistani livestock were subjected to whole-genome sequencing, and complete mitochondrial (mt) genomes were assembled and analyzed using comparative mitogenomics, phylogenetic reconstruction, pairwise genetic distance estimation, and haplotype network analyses. Forty-one H. contortus larvae were successfully characterized for their mitochondrial genomes. The first complete mitochondrial genome of Pakistani H. contortus was 14,002 bp in length and comprised 12 protein-coding genes, 22 transfer RNA genes, and two ribosomal RNA genes, with a marked AT content of 78.37%. Mitochondrial genome organization and gene order were highly conserved relative to published H. contortus mitogenomes. Comparative analyses resolved the Pakistani isolates into two well-supported mitochondrial lineages, while maximum-likelihood phylogenetic analysis clustered all isolates within a robust H. contortus clade clearly distinct from H. placei (bootstrap support, 97-100%). Pairwise genetic distances among Pakistani isolates ranged from 0.00 to 0.05, indicating pronounced nucleotide divergence. Haplotype network analysis identified numerous unique haplotypes together with globally shared haplotypes, supporting substantial mitochondrial diversity. Collectively, these findings provide the first complete mitogenomic resource for H. contortus from Pakistan and advance our understanding of the genetic structure of this economically important veterinary parasite. The generated genomic resource will support molecular epidemiology, population genetic studies, veterinary parasite surveillance, and future investigations of parasite dissemination and anthelmintic resistance in ruminant production systems.

title: Molecular Characterisation of the Romanian African Swine Fever Virus p72 and B602L Genetic Markers.
abstract: African swine fever (ASF) remains one of the most devastating transboundary diseases affecting domestic pigs and wild boars worldwide, making molecular epidemiology essential for understanding viral transmission and supporting disease control. This study aimed to characterise African swine fever virus (ASFV) isolates circulating in Romania through comparative analysis of the B646L (p72) gene and the B602L central variable region (CVR). Fifty-four ASFV-positive samples collected from domestic pigs and wild boars were confirmed by real-time PCR and subjected to molecular analysis. Following Sanger sequencing and sequence quality assessment, 32 reliable consensus sequences were retained for B602L and 33 for p72. Sequencing of the p72 gene demonstrated a very high degree of nucleotide conservation, confirming that all successfully sequenced isolates belonged to genotype II. In contrast, the B602L region exhibited limited intra-genotypic variability characterised by scattered single nucleotide polymorphisms and localised insertion/deletion events, providing additional molecular resolution compared to p72, although insufficient for fine-scale epidemiological tracking. No genetic segregation according to host species was observed for either genomic region, and sequences obtained from domestic pigs and wild boar were interspersed in the phylogenetic analyses, demonstrating a high degree of genetic similarity at the investigated loci. These findings highlight the complementary value of p72 and B602L for ASFV molecular characterisation, while also indicating that these partial genomic markers alone cannot resolve transmission pathways or epidemiological links between domestic and wild host populations.

title: Application Value of In-House HIV-1 DNA Genotypic Resistance Testing for Individuals with Low-Level Viremia.
abstract: To provide evidence for HIV-1 DNA genotypic resistance testing (GRT) strategies in low-level viremia (LLV) populations by comparing the amplification efficiency and resistance mutation profiles between HIV-1 DNA GRT and RNA GRT. (2) Methods: Convenience sampling was used for participant enrolment. Plasma HIV-1 RNA and peripheral blood monocyte (PBMC) DNA were extracted separately. The protease-reverse transcriptase (PR-RT) region was amplified via an in-house protocol, followed by Sanger and Nanopore sequencing. The exact McNemar's test and Fisher's test were applied to compare amplification success rates. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses implemented in R were conducted to identify factors associated with the detection of HIV-1 drug-resistant strains. BEAST-based molecular clock analysis was performed to calculate the divergence time between RNA-derived and DNA-derived sequences. (3) Results: A total of 209 samples were enrolled, and valid sequences were obtained from 166 samples. Within the viral load range of 50-200 copies/mL, HIV-1 DNA GRT yielded significantly higher amplification success rates than RNA GRT (p < 0.05). The overall resistance detection rate for DNA GRT (20.8%) was lower than that for RNA GRT (33.7%), with discrepancies mainly involving nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI)- and non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI)-associated mutations. Individuals receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART) for 7-18 months exhibited higher odds of detecting drug-resistant strains using either DNA GRT or RNA GRT. The median evolutionary divergence time between matched RNA- and DNA-derived sequences was 3.13 years. By contrast, the median evolutionary divergence time between paired DNA generated by Sanger and Nanopore sequencing was 0.84 years. (4) Conclusions: DNA GRT serves as a valuable supplementary screening tool in public health scenarios of LLV with failed RNA GRT amplification. However, clinical interpretation should combine RNA GRT findings, longitudinal viral load monitoring and treatment history, rather than relying solely on DNA GRT to modify antiretroviral regimens.

title: Global Diversity of Norovirus Genotypes from 2002 to 2025: A Review of Temporal, Age-Specific and Regional Trends.
abstract: Norovirus is a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis (AGE) worldwide, with significant morbidity and mortality, particularly in young children and older adults. This study characterizes the global prevalence and diversity of norovirus genotypes among sporadic cases. A review of English-language studies (published 2002-2026) that characterized norovirus genotype distribution among sporadic cases was conducted, excluding outbreak and asymptomatic detections. Pooled data were analyzed with stratifications by age group, region, and year of sample collection. A total of 20,588 cases were identified from 72 publications. There were 30 genotypes identified, with GII.4, GII.3, GII.2, GII.17, and GII.6 and each accounting for ≥5% of detections. GII.4 was the predominant genotype globally, accounting for 54% of cases and up to 80% among older adults across all years, but periodic fluctuation was seen, coinciding with fluctuations in the prevalence of other genotypes, especially GII.3, GII.2, and GII.17. Among GI genotypes, GI.3 was most prevalent (46%), particularly among adults. Genotype diversity was highest among children in low- and middle-income countries and in Asia/Oceania. Findings indicate that a small number of genotypes account for most cases. As genotyping characterizes the major capsid protein, the primary target of antibody recognition, findings have important implications for vaccine development and public health interventions.

title: Hepatitis C Virus Genotype Distribution in Istanbul, Türkiye: Temporal Trends and Demographic Patterns.
abstract: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) genotype distribution varies across geographic regions and populations and may change over time. This study examined the current distribution and temporal trends of HCV genotypes, and their patterns by demographic characteristics and nationality, at a tertiary care hospital in Istanbul, Türkiye. We retrospectively evaluated 188 patients who underwent HCV genotyping between June 2019 and December 2024. Genotype distribution was assessed according to age, sex, and year, while temporal trends were analyzed using the Cochran-Armitage trend test and binomial logistic regression. GT1b was the predominant subtype (54.8%), followed by GT3 (19.1%), GT1a (10.1%), and GT4 (5.9%); mixed-genotype results were detected in 5.9% of cases. Genotype distribution differed significantly by age group and sex (Monte Carlo p = 0.044 and p = 0.002, respectively), but not by year (p = 0.128). After Holm adjustment, GT1a was more frequent among males, whereas GT1b was more frequent among females. No significant linear temporal trends were observed for GT1a, GT1b, GT3, GT4, or mixed-genotype results. Genotype patterns also varied descriptively across nationality groups. These findings underscore the importance of up-to-date regional data and continued genotype surveillance for monitoring changes in HCV epidemiology.

title: Retrospective and Contemporary Genomic Surveillance Reveals Genotype-Specific Dengue Lineage Dynamics in Rio de Janeiro.
abstract: Dengue virus (DENV) transmission in Brazil is characterized by recurrent epidemics involving the introduction, persistence, and replacement of viral lineages. However, temporal gaps in genomic surveillance limit our understanding of how these processes shape successive epidemics in Rio de Janeiro. Here, in a retrospective observational molecular epidemiology study, we combined archived genomic data with publicly available sequences and epidemiological surveillance data to investigate the temporal dynamics of DENV serotypes and lineages in Rio de Janeiro. Archived DENV-positive samples were curated and subjected to whole-genome amplicon sequencing, and the resulting consensus sequences were analyzed together with publicly available sequences using time-scaled phylogenetic reconstruction and epidemiological data. We recovered 35 DENV genomes from samples collected in 2013, 2018, 2020, and 2021, including DENV-1 genotype V, DENV-2 genotypes II and III, and DENV-4 genotype II. Analysis of the combined datasets identified multiple Rio de Janeiro-associated clades with distinct temporal patterns. Publicly available sequences supported the broader clade structure and long-term temporal patterns independently of most genomes generated here. The newly generated genomes made genotype-specific contributions: the five DENV-1 genotype V genomes placed archived 2020-2021 samples within previously represented Rio de Janeiro-associated groups, while the single DENV-2 genotype II genome provided phylogenetic placement of a travel-associated 2018 case. In contrast, the 20 DENV-2 genotype III genomes identified a Rio de Janeiro-associated cluster not represented among the public sequences, and the nine DENV-4 genotype II genomes increased representation of the 2013 epidemic. Thus, the principal contribution of retrospective sequencing was to fill specific temporal and geographic gaps rather than to redefine the broader historical phylogenetic structure of all genotypes.

title: Molecular Evolution of the HMPV-A
abstract: Human metapneumovirus genotype A (HMPV-A) comprises genetically diverse lineages, but whether F-gene diversification is accompanied by changes in the conserved fusion (F) protein remains unclear. We analyzed 500 PARNAS-selected HMPV-A F gene sequences from 25 countries collected between 1982 and 2025 using time-scaled phylogenetics, Bayesian skyline analysis, evolutionary-rate and patristic-distance estimation, codon-based selection analysis, sequence-identity profiling, and structural epitope modeling. Three phylogenetically distinct clusters were identified. Cluster 1 diverged from the common ancestor of Clusters 2 and 3 around 1927. Cluster 3 comprised 435 representative sequences and showed the highest estimated evolutionary rate, greatest phylogenetic diversity, and the most pronounced recent demographic fluctuations. The overall evolutionary rate was 9.20 × 10-4 substitutions/site/year. Despite nucleotide-level diversification, whole-protein identity exceeded 97% in all clusters, 299 codons (approximately 55%) were consistently under negative selection, whereas positive-selection signals were limited and method-specific, with MEME identifying codons 188 and 271 and FUBAR identifying codon 528. Major neutralizing antibody-binding regions were largely conserved, and the six modeled representatives showed similar global F-protein backbone structures and predicted epitope-surface distributions, although A61S and K143T occurred within neutralizing antibody-binding sites and require experimental evaluation. These findings demonstrate lineage-specific F gene diversification under strong functional constraint and support the HMPV F protein as a broadly conserved intervention target.

title: Molecular Epidemiology of Pityriasis Versicolor Reveals a Remarkably High Prevalence of
abstract: Pityriasis versicolor (PV) is a common superficial mycosis caused by lipophilic yeasts of the genus Malassezia. Despite its high prevalence, comprehensive molecular epidemiological data on Malassezia species associated with PV remain limited in several regions of India. Therefore, our study investigated the molecular epidemiology, demographic characteristics, seasonal variation, clinical manifestations, anatomical distribution, and associated predisposing factors among patients with PV from the coastal region of Karnataka. A total of 147 patients clinically diagnosed with PV were included in this study. Skin scrapings were isolated and cultured on lipid-rich media, and isolates were identified using polymerase chain reaction-restriction fragment length polymorphism (PCR-RFLP) and internal transcribed spacer (ITS) sequencing. Molecular identification was performed for 182 Malassezia isolates. Malassezia furfur was the predominant species at 51.1% (93 isolates), followed by Malassezia japonica at 34.1% (62), Malassezia restricta at 5.5% (10), Malassezia slooffiae at 3.3% (6), Malassezia sympodialis at 2.2% (4), Malassezia arunalokei at 2.2% (4), Malassezia globosa at 1.1% (2), and Malassezia pachydermatis at 0.6% (1). In addition, 20 non-Malassezia yeast isolates were identified, including Candida, Rhodotorula, Meyerozyma, and Trichosporon. The study population had a mean age of 27.8 ± 14.9 years, with a male-to-female ratio of 2.2:1. Most cases occurred among individuals aged 10-39 years, while M. furfur remained the predominant species across all age groups and both genders. Seasonal variation was evident, with the highest number of cases recorded during September. Clinically, hypopigmented macules were the predominant lesion type, and the back was the most frequently affected anatomical site. Underlying medical conditions or potential predisposing factors were identified in 18 patients (12.2%), with alcohol-related disorders and immunosuppressive conditions being the most frequently documented. Analyzing all these data, the present study provides updated molecular epidemiological data on Malassezia species causing PV in the coastal region of Karnataka. The predominance of M. furfur and the unexpectedly high prevalence of M. japonica highlight the importance of molecular identification for accurate species-level characterization.

title: Molecular Public Health for Infectious Disease Prevention and Control.
abstract: Molecular technologies have transformed infectious disease surveillance, but their public health value depends on whether molecular signals can be converted into timely and effective action. Unlike molecular epidemiology, which primarily uses molecular variation to characterize distribution, relatedness, transmission, and evolution, molecular public health is defined here as an end-to-end operational framework that connects molecular evidence to population-level decisions, interventions, and evaluation. This narrative review integrates molecular detection, pathogen genomics, bioinformatics, metagenomics, wastewater and environmental surveillance, One Health monitoring, antimicrobial resistance genomics, multi-omics, and artificial intelligence. The framework progresses from detection and analytical interpretation to prediction, intervention, and feedback. Implementation maturity is heterogeneous: targeted PCR, short-read pathogen genomics, and bioinformatics-supported outbreak investigation are established in many defined use cases, whereas pathogen-agnostic metagenomics, multi-omics, and AI-enabled decision support remain more context dependent or emerging. Actionability is operationalized through analytical validity, epidemiological interpretability, sample-to-decision time relative to the intervention window, decision impact, and measurable post-intervention outcomes. Persistent barriers include sampling bias, uneven global capacity, incomplete metadata, insufficient standardization, governance concerns, and poorly defined trigger thresholds. The central criterion for the field should therefore be whether molecular information measurably improves prevention and control.

title: Antimicrobial Resistance in
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is an important One Health challenge, yet evidence on resistant Escherichia coli and Salmonella spp. in Romania is dispersed across animal species, food matrices, environmental compartments, and surveillance systems. This comprehensive narrative review synthesizes and critically evaluates evidence across animal-food-environment interfaces and places it in the context of broader European AMR patterns. Particular attention is given to isolate origin, resistance phenotypes, multidrug resistance, major resistance determinants, molecular epidemiology, and the strength of evidence supporting cross-sector connections. Studies most frequently addressed poultry and swine, where resistance to ampicillin, fluoroquinolones, sulfonamides, and tetracyclines was repeatedly reported, together with extended-spectrum cephalosporin resistance, particularly in E. coli. Evidence from cattle, foods of animal origin, companion animals, wildlife, wastewater, and aquatic environments shows that resistant bacteria and antimicrobial resistance genes occur across multiple compartments. Substantial heterogeneity in sampling design, susceptibility testing, and molecular characterization limits direct comparison between studies, while epidemiologically linked investigations and whole-genome sequencing across connected reservoirs remain uncommon. Priorities include more standardized cross-sector surveillance, stronger environmental monitoring, expanded genomic epidemiology, improved data interoperability, and continued antimicrobial stewardship. By integrating fragmented national evidence, this review identifies both well-characterized sectors and interfaces where important evidence gaps remain.

title: Nirsevimab in the New Era of RSV Prevention: Current Evidence, Emerging Challenges, and Future Perspectives.
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the leading cause of lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) and hospitalization in infants and young children worldwide, with the highest disease burden occurring in otherwise healthy term infants during the first 6 months of life. The recent introduction of long-acting monoclonal antibodies and maternal RSV vaccination has fundamentally changed preventive strategies against severe RSV disease. Evidence from randomized clinical trials and large real-world studies consistently demonstrates that a single dose of Nirsevimab provides season-long protection against RSV-associated LRTI and reduces hospitalization rate across diverse infant populations, while maintaining an excellent safety profile. Emerging data also support its effectiveness in routine clinical practice, although important uncertainties remain regarding long-term epidemiological effects, viral evolution, resistance, comparative effectiveness with maternal immunization, and optimal implementation across different healthcare settings. Current evidence supports Nirsevimab as a major advance in infant RSV prevention. However, continued surveillance, comparative effectiveness studies, and equitable global implementation will be essential to maximize its long-term public health impact. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on Nirsevimab, with emphasis on its clinical efficacy, safety, real-world effectiveness, resistance, implementation challenges, cost-effectiveness, and its role alongside maternal RSV vaccination.

title: Beyond Resistance: Carbapenemase Gene Profiles and Mortality in ICU Patients with Carbapenem-Resistant
abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) causes serious infections in intensive care units (ICUs), but the relationship between carbapenemase gene profiles and mortality remains uncertain. This prospective two-center cohort included 94 adult ICU patients with clinical CRKP infection from April to September 2026. The first clinical isolate from each patient was included. blaKPC, blaNDM, blaVIM, blaIMP, blaOXA-48, and blaCTX-M genes were investigated by polymerase chain reaction. The primary outcome was 28-day ICU mortality; 14-day and final ICU mortality were secondary outcomes. blaOXA-48, blaNDM, blaKPC, and blaCTX-M were detected in 65 (69.1%), 49 (52.1%), 19 (20.2%), and 73 (77.7%) of isolates, respectively; blaNDM and blaOXA-48 co-occurred in 39 (41.5%). Fourteen-day, 28-day, and final ICU mortality rates occured in 38 (40.4%), 48 (51.1%), and 53 (56.4%), respectively. No statistically significant associations were observed between individual genes, the presence of two carbapenemase genes, or carbapenemase profiles and any mortality endpoint; adjusted analyses of 28-day ICU mortality yielded similar findings. In the exploratory Firth model, the profile effect was not significant (p = 0.198), whereas a higher age-adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index and bloodstream infection or ventilator-associated pneumonia, compared with urinary tract infection, were associated with higher odds of 28-day ICU mortality. Frequent gene co-occurrence was observed; however, clinically meaningful gene-mortality associations cannot be excluded because of imprecise estimates.

title: Variant-Specific Temporal Transcriptomic Responses of Ex Vivo Dog Lung Explants to SARS-CoV-2 Delta and Omicron Infection.
abstract: The rapid evolution and emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants have posed significant public health challenges due to enhanced transmissibility and diverse clinical outcomes. While the effects of these variants in humans have been extensively investigated, their impact on domestic animals remains insufficiently understood. Given the close interaction between humans and dogs, along with documented cases of human-to-animal transmission and the potential role of companion animals as reservoirs for viral evolution, understanding the molecular dynamics of SARS-CoV-2 infection in dogs is of considerable importance. However, in vivo infection studies in non-laboratory animal species are highly resource intensive, time-consuming, require ABSL3 facilities, and involve ethical constraints, limiting their widespread application. In this context, ex vivo culture systems provide a practical and physiologically relevant alternative. Therefore, in the present study, we employed an ex vivo lung explant culture model derived from domestic dogs to investigate host responses to the SARS-CoV-2 Delta and Omicron variants. Comprehensive transcriptomic profiling across multiple time points post-infection revealed significant alterations in genes associated with cell adhesion, structural components, extracellular matrix (ECM) organization and regulation, immune responses, mitochondrial activity, oxidative phosphorylation, and ribosomal function. Both variants induced marked downregulation of ECM-associated and T-cell-related genes, suggesting disruption of tissue integrity and suppression of adaptive immune responses. The Delta variant was characterized by early and sustained suppression of immune-associated signaling pathways, particularly T-cell receptor signaling, whereas the Omicron variant induced stronger activation of genes associated with mitochondrial activity, oxidative phosphorylation, and translational responses. At later stages of infection, especially at 24 h post-infection (hpi), canine lung explants exhibited increased expression of genes related to tissue repair, epithelial maintenance, mitochondrial function, and ribosomal activity, suggesting activation of compensatory responses aimed at maintaining cellular stability under viral stress. Notably, several hub genes were identified, including CD2, CD3D, CD3E, CD27, PTPRC, ZAP70, SYK, and LCP2 in Delta infection, and FLT3LG, MRPL2, MRPL4, MRPS11, MRPS12, RPS13, and RPS5 in Omicron infection, which are involved in critical pathways associated with immune signaling, mitochondrial function, metabolic regulation, and protein synthesis. Furthermore, the observed mitochondrial and ribosomal responses may indicate that therapeutic strategies aimed at supporting mitochondrial function and modulating excessive inflammation could potentially help reduce lung damage during severe infection. Overall, this study provides important insights into the transcriptomic response of dog lung explants following exposure to SARS-CoV-2 Delta and Omicron variants and also highlights the utility of ex vivo canine lung explant cultures as a valuable platform for studying host-pathogen interactions.

title: First Report of Molecular Prevalence and Genetic Characterization of
abstract: Enterocytozoon bieneusi is an important microsporidian pathogen with a broad host range and potential zoonotic relevance, yet molecular data from cattle in Romania are lacking. This study investigated, for the first time, the molecular prevalence, genotype diversity, and phylogenetic relationships of E. bieneusi in young dairy cattle in western Romania. A total of 190 fecal samples were collected from young dairy cattle, comprising pre-weaned calves and post-weaned cattle up to 12 months of age from 28 farms in Arad and Timiș counties and examined by nested PCR targeting the internal transcribed spacer (ITS) region of the rRNA gene. E. bieneusi DNA was detected in 27/190 cattle, corresponding to an overall prevalence of 14.2% (95% CI: 10.0-19.9%). Pre-weaned cattle showed a higher prevalence than post-weaned animals (18.1% vs. 8.1%), but the difference was not statistically significant (OR = 2.51, 95% CI: 0.96-6.54; p = 0.058). High-quality ITS sequences were obtained from 20 positive samples, revealing five established genotypes, namely BEB4 (45.0%), I (25.0%), J (10.0%), BEB8 (10.0%), and BEB17 (10.0%), among the genotyped isolates (n = 20). Phylogenetic analysis placed all Romanian isolates within Group 2, predominantly associated with ruminants but also containing genotypes reported in humans. These findings establish the first molecular baseline for E. bieneusi in young dairy cattle in western Romania and provide initial information on their epidemiological relevance within a One Health framework.

title: Anticipating the Next Recorded Bacterial Hosts of Plasmid-Borne Antimicrobial Resistance Genes: A Temporal Graph Analysis of Plasmid and Surveillance Data.
abstract: Plasmid-mediated dissemination of antimicrobial resistance genes complicates the control of bacterial infections. Identifying bacterial hosts likely to harbour these genes could guide genomic surveillance before such associations enter public databases. We investigated whether existing plasmid and surveillance data could anticipate which resistance gene-host associations would next be recorded in those databases, and which genomic features inform that prediction. We integrated 72,556 complete plasmid records and 2,116,241 surveillance isolates, encompassing 458 resistance gene alleles, 574 replicon backbones and 222 bacterial species. A temporal graph model, MobiGraph, was trained on associations recorded before a fixed cutoff and evaluated on subsequently observed associations, using candidate hosts matched for sequencing effort and phylogenetic distance. Ranking within a candidate pool was the primary outcome; threshold-free summaries are reported as secondary. The observed host ranked among the ten highest-priority candidates in 42.4% of test cases; the advantage over gradient boosting on mechanistic features was confined to the ranking metrics, the two being indistinguishable on area under the precision-recall curve. Plasmid incompatibility-group compatibility, previous gene-host associations and shared relaxase classes were prominent predictive features. Across five resistance determinants, including mcr-1, blaNDM and tet(X4), 43-62% of subsequent associations were ranked within the top ten. Among recovered events, the median interval from the prediction cutoff to first recorded observation was 22.5 months. In a separate evaluation of a fixed 500-entry watch list, 65 entries were subsequently recorded as gene-host pairs over 25 months, 13.0% against an 8.2% background rate (95% CI 10.3-16.2%); because the surveillance database does not resolve the replicon, this confirmation does not extend to the predicted backbone. Existing plasmid and genomic surveillance records contain information that can help anticipate which resistance gene-host associations will next be recorded. Whether a newly recorded association reflects recent transfer or earlier under-sampling cannot be resolved from these data. These findings support prioritising bacterial hosts for targeted surveillance and experimental investigation of plasmid-mediated resistance dissemination.

title: Antimicrobial Resistance and Molecular Epidemiology of Haemophilus influenzae Causing Pediatric Acute Otitis Media in Japan.
abstract: Antimicrobial-resistant strains of Haemophilus influenzae are associated with treatment failure and recurrence in acute otitis media (AOM). We aimed to characterize the current antimicrobial susceptibility of H. influenzae isolates from children with AOM, elucidate β-lactam and quinolone resistance mechanisms, and determine the molecular epidemiology of resistant strains. We analyzed 182 H. influenzae isolates from the middle ear fluid of children aged ≤3 years with AOM from multiple regions in Japan (February 2022-May 2023). Antimicrobial susceptibility was tested, and β-lactamase genes (blaTEM-1 and blaROB-1) were detected. Sequence analyses of ftsI, encoding PBP3 and quinolone resistance-determining regions were performed to elucidate the resistance mechanisms. Multilocus sequence typing (MLST) was conducted for the ampicillin- and quinolone-low-susceptible strains. Of 182 isolates, 14 (7.7%), 10 (5.5%), 36 (19.8%) and 122 (67.0%) were β-lactamase-producing, β-lactamase-nonproducing ampicillin-resistant (BLNAR), low-BLNAR and β-lactamase-nonproducing ampicillin-susceptible strains, respectively. All 10 BLNAR and 4 β-lactamase-producing isolates exhibited group III PBP3 amino acid substitutions associated with high-level resistance. MLST revealed genetic diversity among BLNAR isolates, whereas 7 (50.0%) β-lactamase-producing isolates belonged to ST103, indicating clonal dissemination. Amino acid substitutions in the quinolone resistance-determining region were detected in six quinolone-low-susceptible strains; these isolates exhibited diverse STs. The β-lactam susceptibility of H. influenzae isolates causing pediatric AOM exhibited an overall improvement. However, an increasing trend in quinolone-low-susceptible strains was observed. Specific clones represented by ST103 were detected among some of the β-lactamase-producing strains, warranting careful monitoring.

title: Clinical significance of different
abstract: Histoplasmosis is recognized as endemic in Québec; however, no molecular epidemiological studies have been conducted to date. The clinical significance of identifying Histoplasma capsulatum genotypes remains unclear. We performed a retrospective multicenter study of 67 culture-confirmed histoplasmosis cases from four major academic hospitals in Québec between 1988 and 2014. Multi-locus sequence typing (MLST) was performed on isolates, and clinical data were analyzed for genotype-specific associations with demographics, clinical presentations, and outcomes. Most isolates belonged to either the North American clade 2 (48.1%) or Latin American clade A (39.2%), highlighting both endemic and imported disease patterns in Québec. A novel NAm2 sequence type (ST81) was identified, which was unique to Québec and accounted for 61% of the NAm2 isolates, but was not associated with significantly different clinical outcomes compared with other NAm2 strains. In multivariate analysis, disseminated disease was independently associated with immunosuppression (OR 14.18, P = 0.001), male sex (OR 6.01, P = 0.035), and LAmA genotype (OR 5.02, P = 0.031). Severe outcomes (intensive care unit admission, intubation, death, or amphotericin B use) were associated with immunosuppression (OR 4.48, P = 0.023), with a non-significant trend with LAmA infections (OR 3.06, P = 0.069). This first molecular characterization of histoplasmosis infections in Québec suggests a dual epidemiology, with locally acquired NAm2 and LAmA infections more often associated with travel or origin from endemic regions outside Québec. Host factors were associated with disease severity, while the potential contribution of fungal genotype requires further study. These findings highlight the value of molecular characterization for understanding the epidemiology of histoplasmosis in endemic settings. Histoplasmosis is an important dimorphic fungal infection in North America. Although Québec is a recognized endemic region, its molecular epidemiology has not been previously characterized, and the clinical relevance of different Histoplasma genotypes remains uncertain. In this multicenter study, we performed multi-locus sequence typing with detailed clinical data from 67 culture-confirmed cases diagnosed between 1988 and 2014. This represents the first molecular characterization of clinical Histoplasma isolates from Québec and the largest Canadian cohort examining the association between molecular genotypes, clinical presentation, and outcomes. We identified both North American NAm2 (Histoplasma ohiense) and imported Latin American LAmA (Histoplasma suramericanum) lineages, suggestive of a combination of locally acquired and travel-associated infections. We also identified a novel NAm2 sequence type (ST81) that appears unique to Québec, suggesting possible regional circulation. The LAmA genotype was associated with disseminated histoplasmosis, whereas immunosuppression was the principal predictor of severe outcomes. Overall, host factors were associated with disease severity, while the potential contribution of fungal genotype warrants further study. These findings highlight the value of molecular characterization for understanding the epidemiology of histoplasmosis in endemic settings.

title: Molecular Epidemiology of Varicella-Zoster Virus Among Patients From Two French Tertiary Care Hospitals: Differential Distribution of Clades According to Demographic Criteria.
abstract: Varicella-zoster virus (VZV) nomenclature currently recognizes seven established clades (designated 1-6 and 9). A geographical segregation of VZV clades has been shown, with Clades 1, 3, and 6 predominating in Europe, Americas, and Australia, Clade 2 in Japan and East-Asia, and Clades 4 and 5 in Asia and Africa. This distribution of VZV clades is dependent on the importation of viral strains, because of immigration and travels, and the implementation of varicella vaccine. The surveillance of VZV epidemiology is therefore necessary. VZV genotyping strategies rely on evaluating a panel of single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) across the different open reading frames (ORFs) of the viral genome. We described retrospectively the VZV clade distribution among 339 patients in Pitié-Salpêtrière (Paris) and Bordeaux University hospitals from 2018 to 2023. Clade 1 was detected in 27.1%, Clade 3 in 37.2%, Clade 5 in 31.9%, and other clades in 3.8% of the patients. The distribution of clades did not differ according to sex, immune status of the patients, and clinical presentation of VZV infection. However, patients infected with Clade 5 were statistically younger than those infected with other clades, especially European-born patients. This epidemiological characteristic of VZV Clade 5 may have multifactorial etiology, including the combination of viral, host, and environmental factors.

title: Evolving genetic landscapes of Plasmodium falciparum Kelch13 polymorphisms in Nigeria: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Malaria incidence has plateaued in recent years, with periodic increases observed in some settings. This trend is driven by multiple factors, including health system disruptions, vector and parasite resistance, and environmental changes. The emergence of partial resistance to artemisinin-based combination therapies (ACTs) has contributed to delayed parasite clearance and, in some regions, treatment failure. Hence, the need to study the polymorphisms in the Plasmodium falciparum Kelch13 gene from studies conducted in Nigeria and imported malaria cases from Nigeria reported in other countries. The systematic review and meta-analysis employed the population, intervention or test, comparison, and outcome (PICO) and preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses (PRISMA) guidelines to formulate the research questions and report the reviewed articles completely in both the studies in Nigeria and imported Plasmodium falciparum kelch-13 (Pfk13) studies from Nigeria reported in other countries. The review included studies that contained any kind of mutation in the Pfk13 gene from P. falciparum and excluded reports for mutations of other antimalarial resistance. The reviewed articles were generated from PubMed, Springer Nature, and Google Scholar using the litsearchr and metagear packages in R. Heterogeneity analyses for the articles and reported SNPs were carried out. Furthermore, the ordinary least squares (OLS) network model was used to assess the effect of distance on Pfk13 SNP occurrence, while the geostatistical model was used to predict the frequency of Pfk13 SNP in the country. In Nigeria, about 124 different Pfk13 single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) have been reported, which are predominantly non-synonymous mutants domiciled in the kelch-13 propeller domain. The studies were heterogeneous in reporting SNPs occurrence ( I 2 = 95.3%, τ 2 = 0.0683, p < 0.0001), and no dominant SNP was reported from the pooled studies ( I 2 = 36.0%, τ 2 < 0.0001, p < 0.0001). The network model showed no correlation between the spatial locations of the states and the similarity of their Pfk13 alleles ( β = 0.00035, p = 0.51), with high nucleotide diversity ( π = 2.31) of the Pfk13 SNPs. A total of three validated (C580Y, F446I, and A675V) and one candidate (R515K) Pfk13 SNPs were present from the various reports, and the predicted Pfk13 mutation frequency showed a marginally higher occurrence in the Southeast and South-South regions of the country and Lagos State. Highly diverse and independent emergence of Pfk13 SNPs together with those that are responsible for artemisinin partial resistance has been reported in Nigeria. These patterns underscore the urgent need for sustained Pfk13 genomic surveillance and ACT therapeutic efficacy studies to preempt and mitigate the establishment and spread of artemisinin- and partner drug-resistant strains in the country.

To investigate the molecular mechanisms driving rapid spread of HIV-1 CRF59_01B and CRF55_01B among men who have sex with men (MSM) in China and the molecular evolution and dispersal pathways of ΔKSKK deletion and KSKK→KSQQ substitution mutations in HIV-1 Gagp17 protein. The characteristic mutations of Gagp17 protein in the CRF59_01B and CRF55_01B strains were analyzed. HIV-1 mutant plasmids carrying the ΔKSKK deletion mutation and KSKK→KSQQ substitution mutation were constructed and their effects on viral release and maturation were evaluated. Spatiotemporal diffusion maps and key transmission chains of the two mutations were reconstructed using Bayesian discrete phylogeographic analysis. Compared with HIV-1 subtype B, 9 out of 10 CRF59_01B strains carried a deletion mutation of amino acids 110-113 (ΔKSKK deletion) in the Gagp17 protein, while 23 out of 29 CRF55_01B strains had a KSKK→KSQQ mutation. Compared with the wild-type virus, the ΔKSKK deletion and KSKK→KSQQ substitution mutants showed increased Gagp24 protein levels in cell culture supernatants by 173% and 99%, increased viral release efficiency to 161% and 152%, and enhanced Gag protein cleavage efficiency by 47% and 64%, respectively, with also increased proportions of viruses with a typical cone-shaped core (from 18% to 25%-27%). Molecular evolutionary analysis suggested that the ΔKSKK deletion mutation originated in southern Africa around 1938 (P=0.832), then spread to Asia with Australia as the intercontinental hub and China as a "bridge" in the transmission chain; The KSKK→KSQQ substitution mutation originated in Zambia around 1929 (P=0.918) and spread to China, then to the Americas, Europe, and Asia with Thailand and Australia as transmission hubs. The KSKK→KSQQ substitution and ΔKSKK deletion mutations in Gagp17 protein characteristic of HIV-1 CRF55_01B and CRF59_01B strains result in enhanced viral replication and infectivity by modulating HIV-1 viral release and Gag protein cleavage maturation.

title: Molecular epidemiology of dengue virus in the Bangka Belitung Islands, Indonesia, during the COVID-19 pandemic.
abstract: Dengue virus (DENV) infection poses a major global health challenge with a rising number of infections worldwide. In Indonesia, molecular epidemiological studies have been limited, focusing primarily on Java Island, which has led to a sufficiency in comprehensive data of DENV characteristics. During the COVID-19 pandemic, fewer DENV epidemiological studies were conducted, further leaving a gap in our understanding of viral circulation during this period. Characterization of DENV serotypes, genotypes, and nucleotide substitutions is essential for improving clinical management and informing vaccine strategies. This study employed a cross-sectional design with consecutive sampling of suspected dengue patients from a private clinic and hospital in Bangka-Belitung, Indonesia, between 2019 and 2023. Patients with fever and two or more clinical symptoms of DENV infection were included. DENV infection was confirmed by NS1 antigen test, and positive samples were further analyzed for DENV serotypes by RT-PCR, followed by envelope gene analysis for phylogenetic characterization. Out of 92 suspected dengue infections, 74 cases (80.43%) were confirmed for DENV infection via RT-PCR, NS-1, or IgM antibody tests, with the majority of confirmed dengue cases occurred in children. DENV-3 was found to be the most dominant serotype (38.71%), followed by DENV-1 (11.83%), which aligns with previous studies characterizing the serotypes of circulating DENV strains. Phylogenetic analysis of DENV (1-4) during the COVID-19 pandemic revealed that these strains clustered into a distinct groups under the same genotypes as earlier outbreaks. This molecular epidemiology and seroprevalence data provide valuable insight into the circulating DENV strains in Indonesia. AUTHOR SUMMARY: Dengue virus (DENV) remains a major public health problem in Indonesia, one of the countries with the highest dengue burden worldwide. Although DENV is endemic throughout the Indonesian archipelago, information on the genetic diversity and circulation of DENV is still limited in many regions outside Java Island. Bangka Belitung Province is an understudied area where molecular epidemiological data are largely unavailable, making it difficult to understand local transmission patterns and support evidence-based control strategies. In this study, we investigated DENV infections in Bangka Belitung before and during the COVID-19 pandemic. We analyzed clinical samples from patients with suspected DENV infection to determine circulating serotypes and genetic characteristics of the virus. All four DENV serotypes were detected, with DENV-3 identified as the predominant serotype throughout the study period. Phylogenetic analyses showed that the circulating viruses belonged to genotypes that have been reported previously in Indonesia, indicating ongoing endemic transmission and genetic diversity within the country. Our findings provide the first comprehensive molecular epidemiological data on DENV circulation in Bangka Belitung. These results contribute to a better understanding of dengue transmission dynamics in Indonesia and highlight the importance of continuous molecular surveillance to detect viral introductions, monitor genetic changes, and support DENV prevention and control programs.
journal: Infection, genetics and evolution : journal of molecular epidemiology and evolutionary genetics in infectious diseases

title: Genetic diversity of inclusion body hepatitis-associated fowl adenoviruses in Thailand from 2014 to 2025.
abstract: Inclusion body hepatitis (IBH), caused by fowl adenoviruses (FAdVs), is an important disease affecting poultry health and production. Limited cross-protection among heterologous FAdV serotypes makes molecular surveillance essential for guiding disease prevention and control. Nevertheless, serotype distribution and genetic diversity of IBH-associated FAdVs in Thailand remain limited. To address this gap, a retrospective molecular study analyzed 56 FAdV-positive chickens associated with IBH or suspected IBH that were submitted for diagnostic investigation between 2014 and 2025. A partial hexon L1-loop region was amplified, sequenced, and analyzed by phylogenetic and deduced amino-acid comparisons. The isolates were classified into three serotypes: FAdV-8b, FAdV-11, and FAdV-2. FAdV-8b was the most frequently detected serotype, accounting for 30/56 isolates (53.57%), followed by FAdV-11 with 23/56 isolates (41.07%) and FAdV-2 with 3/56 isolates (5.36%). Temporal differences in serotype distribution were observed among the sequenced diagnostic submissions. All sequences collected during 2014-2018 belonged to species D and included FAdV-2 and FAdV-11. FAdV-8b was first detected in this dataset in 2019, and it accounted for 30 of the 35 sequences obtained during 2019-2025. Phylogenetic analysis separated Thai FAdV-8b isolates into three groups and FAdV-2 isolates into two groups, while FAdV-11 isolates were highly conserved within the analyzed region. Group-associated amino-acid substitutions were mainly located in the hypervariable regions of the Hexon L1-loop, suggesting potential relevance to within-serotype antigenic variation. Overall, these findings provide updated molecular epidemiological information on IBH-associated FAdVs in Thailand and underscore the need for continued molecular surveillance to inform diagnostic strategies and vaccine selection.
